title: Fix the `CollectionProxy#delete_all` documentation return value
body:
`CollectionProxy#delete_all` returns the number of deleted records, but the example for the default `:nullify` strategy shows it returning an array of the records themselves:

```ruby
person.pets.delete_all
# => [
#       #<Pet id: 1, name: "Fancy-Fancy", person_id: 1>,
#       #<Pet id: 2, name: "Spook", person_id: 1>,
#       #<Pet id: 3, name: "Choo-Choo", person_id: 1>
#    ]
```

The test suite asserts the count for this exact strategy:

```ruby
# activerecord/test/cases/associations/has_many_associations_test.rb
assert_equal count, firm.dependent_clients_of_firm.delete_all(:nullify)
```

Three deletion strategies are documented on this method, and `:nullify` is the only one that still shows an array. The equivalent lines were removed from the `:destroy` and `:delete_all` examples in 9534006c47 and 02d3a25361.

9534006c47 also dropped the "Returns an array with the deleted records." sentence from the prose, but the correct return value was not added back. This restores it so the summary now reads the same way as the neighbouring `#delete` and `#destroy`, which both document theirs:

```ruby
# #delete
# ... then it will follow the default strategy. Returns an array with the
# deleted records.

# #delete_all (this change)
# ... then it will follow the default strategy. Returns the number of deleted
# records.
```

`delete_all` is the only one of the four deletion methods on `CollectionProxy` that does not return records, which is what made the stale example misleading in the first place (see #14546).

title: Fix live reloader deadlock
body:
### Motivation / Background We encountered #56888 while using `ActionController::Live` to implement GraphQL `@defer`, following [graphql-ruby's streaming response documentation](https://graphql-ruby.org/defer/setup#sending-streaming-responses). In development (with class unloading enabled), Live requests could occasionally deadlock with a reload. This is because `ActionController::Live` schedules the controller action on a child thread while the request thread retains its running Share and waits for the response to commit. If an unload queues before the child acquires its own Share, `ShareLock`'s writer preference blocks the child behind the unload: 1. The unload waits for the request thread to release its Share. 2. The request thread waits for the Live child to commit the response. 3. The Live child waits behind the unload. This forms a cycle in which none of the participants can proceed.
(a more visual version of the deadlock timeline, if it's helpful) ```text P = original Live request thread C = Live child thread U = request performing the unload P: Live request C: Live child U: Reload request --------------- ------------- ----------------- acquire running Share schedule C scheduled, but has not run yet wait for response commit acquire running Share request Exclusive unload lock yield its own running Share wait for P to release its Share request running Share blocked behind U by writer preference ``` At this point: ```text P waits for C to commit the response C waits for U's unload U waits for P to release its running Share ``` ![deadlock](https://media4.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExc3BnMWY4YjkweWZxdjR3cnYyN2x2Z3A1Y2p4N29meGVnbmJsYWx2eiZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/UAHZijO91QCl2/giphy.gif)
Fixes #56888 🤞 ### Detail This adds one-shot sharing continuations to `ShareLock`. Work scheduled by an existing Share owner can claim its own ordinary Share ahead of an Exclusive waiter that queued afterward. A pending continuation keeps the lock busy for Exclusive acquisition, closing the gap between scheduling the work and the child execution context acquiring its Share. Once claimed, the continuation holds an ordinary Share for the full duration of its block. This priority is limited: * Unrelated new sharers remain blocked behind queued Exclusive waiters. * An Exclusive lock that has already been acquired still takes precedence. * A continuation can only be claimed once. * If scheduling raises, its pending continuation is canceled. `ActionController::Live#process` now schedules its child action through an interlock continuation, associating that work with the request that was already admitted before the unload queued. The added coverage includes focused `ShareLock` tests and a deterministic Live regression that pauses the child before it claims its continuation, queues an unload, and verifies that the child commits the response before the unload begins. The Live regression fails on `main`, and passes with this change. The external [reproduction application](https://github.com/GetJobber/reproduce-rails-deadlock-behaviour) I made last time also completed ten consecutive runs without request timeouts. ### Additional information I previously proposed a smaller fix in [#56942](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/56942). That approach breaks the deadlock by allowing the unload to overtake the Live child. This can leave a controller instance created before the unload executing after application constants have been reloaded, potentially mixing code from different generations. The continuation approach instead treats the child as work admitted with its parent request, ensuring it begins before a later unload while retaining its own execution-context-owned Share. ### Checklist Before submitting the PR make sure the following are checked: * [x] This Pull Request is related to one change. Unrelated changes should be opened in separate PRs. * [x] Commit message has a detailed description of what changed and why. If this PR fixes a related issue include it in the commit message. Ex: `[Fix #issue-number]` * [x] Tests are added or updated if you fix a bug or add a feature. * [x] CHANGELOG files are updated for the changed libraries if there is a behavior change or additional feature. Minor bug fixes and documentation changes should not be included.

title: Honour `all_queries` default scopes in internal queries
body:
### Motivation / Background

Apply `all_queries` default scopes to internal queries, like uniqueness validations, fixture loading, and counter caches.

Extracted from: https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/57123

> We also audited places that call unscope but should be respecting all-queries scopes. We added the all_queries_scopes method to uniqueness validations, fixture loading and updating/reseting counter caches.

### Detail

Introduces an `all_queries_scope` method to build an internal query scope. It applies:
  - Default scopes with all_queries: true.
  - The current scope from scoping(all_queries: true).

It excludes ordinary default scopes.

### Additional information

There are ongoing discussions on whether the durable scopes change will be landed, so these changes should be shipped separately.

### Checklist

Before submitting the PR make sure the following are checked:

* [X] This Pull Request is related to one change. Unrelated changes should be opened in separate PRs.
